problem_statement:
Module attribute patching not working after freeze_time start

#### Description

When using freeze_time, modules imported after starting the freeze are not getting their time-related attributes properly patched with fake implementations. This causes datetime, time, and other time-related functions to return real time values instead of the frozen time.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import sys
import datetime
from freezegun import freeze_time

# Make sure module isn't already imported
if 'some_module' in sys.modules:
    del sys.modules['some_module']

with freeze_time('2012-01-14'):
    # Import module after freeze_time has started
    import some_module_with_datetime_usage
    
    # These should return frozen time but return real time instead
    print(some_module_with_datetime_usage.get_current_time())  # Returns real time
    print(datetime.datetime.now())  # Returns frozen time (works correctly)
```

The issue appears when modules are imported after `freeze_time` has already started. The time-related attributes in these newly imported modules are not being replaced with their fake counterparts, causing them to use real time functions instead of the frozen time implementations.

This affects various time-related functions including `datetime.datetime`, `time.time`, `time.localtime`, `time.gmtime`, and `time.strftime` when accessed through module attributes that were imported after the freeze began.
